messages:
ciara: running into a weird error when I import the JS SDK in a Cloudflare Worker — auth requests fail with 'crypto.createHmac is not a function'. anyone seen this?
ben: yep, classic Node vs Web runtime mismatch. CF Workers use WebCrypto (subtle) not node:crypto. the SDK's auth helper still calls createHmac in the CJS runtime path.
omar: are you running the bundled esm build or pulling cjs by accident? package.json exports can accidentally resolve to the wrong entry for some bundlers.
ciara: using snowpack -> it ended up resolving to the cjs entry. how do we fix this for edge users without forcing them to bundle differently?
marta: options: 1) publish a dedicated "edge" entrypoint that uses WebCrypto and no node APIs, 2) provide a tiny runtime shim that implements createHmac via WebCrypto for Workers, or 3) update package.json exports to prefer the browser/edge field so bundlers pick the right file.
ben: +1 for a proper edge build. shims are ok short-term but brittle. we should also add a runtime check and better error message when node crypto is referenced in an edge runtime.
ciara: example shim I slapped together (worked for me):
```js
// workers-crypto-shim.js
export async function createHmac(key, data, algo = 'SHA-256') {
  const keyObj = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', new TextEncoder().encode(key), {name: 'HMAC', hash: {name: algo}}, false, ['sign']);
  const sig = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', keyObj, new TextEncoder().encode(data));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(sig)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}
```
ciara: then I `replace` the auth call at build time with that shim. hacky but unblocks work.
omar: can we avoid users needing that? devex SDK should export an edge-compatible bundle. propose `dist/edge/index.mjs` that uses WebCrypto and no Buffer, fs, net, etc. put conditional exports in package.json:```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "browser": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
  }
}
```
ben: plus add `"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"` and `typesVersions` so TS users on edge get correct types. Some TypeScript tooling still resolves cjs d.ts if we don't provide explicit mapping.
marta: note: some bundlers (older rollup configs) ignore `exports.edge` and prefer `import`. we should also update our docs and the SDK quickstart: `import {createClient} from 'redwood-sdk/edge'` as an explicit opt-in path.
ciara: quick question re: retries — our auth wrapper uses `setTimeout` + `AbortController`. CF Workers have AbortController but timer behavior can differ. any gotchas?
ben: setTimeout exists but long-running timers are throttle-limited. better to use a backoff loop that uses fetch timeouts via AbortController.signal and short delays. avoid relying on Node's `timers/promises` API.
omar: and streaming: Workers support ReadableStream for responses but many Node libs expect Node streams. avoid returning Node stream instances from SDK; normalize to Web Streams in the edge build.
marta: typing note: some code uses `Buffer` in d.ts (e.g. Buffer | Uint8Array). prefer `Uint8Array` in edge types and add a small compatibility typedef for `EdgeBuffer = Uint8Array` in our types folder.
ciara: thanks — i'll try the dist/edge import and file a small PR to add better runtime detection + a clear error message recommending the edge bundle.
ben: please also add a CI smoke test that runs the edge bundle in Miniflare (CF worker local) so we catch regressions.
deploy-bot: CI test 'edge-bundle-miniflare' queued by ciara at 2026-11-02T15:22:00Z :rocket:
marta: note for the RFC — we should document common polyfills users reach for: Buffer, node:crypto, fs (not available), net/socket (not available). add a troubleshooting page with minimal shims and example package.json export snippet.
ciara: i'll draft the troubleshooting doc and link to the shim snippet + recommended package.json mapping. posting soon. :pray:
